transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-07
Time: 10:00am PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez (Redwood); Emily Park, Rajesh Singh, Sophie Martin (NexaHealth)

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok, hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is our weekly POC sync for NexaHealth. quick agenda: onboarding progress, access, env readiness, and then we'll review next steps.
[00:12] Emily Park: yeah thanks Maya, we got your invite, happy to go through. just to note Rajesh is with network and Sophie is on security for any compliance questions.
[00:24] Diego Alvarez: hi all, Diego here, i'll be running the perf tests and helping with model configuration during the pilot.
[00:30] Sophie Martin: morning. just a quick callout - we need the SOC2 artifact and encryption details before we enable any data syncs.
[00:40] Maya Chen: absolutely, i'll send the SAML and SOC2 docs after this call, and a short SOW for the pilot.
[00:46] Rajesh Singh: on the network side we are prepping VPC peering, i've got a couple questions around IP ranges and egress.

[00:58] Maya Chen: great, for the peering we're expecting a small set of CIDRs - we'll provide the egress endpoints, but plan is to keep traffic locked to the us-west2 region. Diego, can you confirm the endpoints again?
[01:12] Diego Alvarez: sure, it's the rwinf-prod-1.us-west2.redwood-inference.internal and the control plane endpoint at control.redwood.io, but i'll send a short list with IPs. also note we have ephemeral egress for model pulls during cold starts.
[01:29] Rajesh Singh: okay, ephemeral model pulls - that's fine as long as we can allow those IPs. what about auth? we prefer cross-account IAM roles or SAML.
[01:40] Maya Chen: SAML SSO is supported and we also offer assume-role for cloud integrations. Sophie, the keys are customer managed in the Private offering - we can discuss KMS/HSM options.
[01:52] Sophie Martin: got it. do you log token-level usage? we need audit logs retained for 90 days.
[01:58] Maya Chen: yes, in Redwood Console you can enable audit logs and set retention - i'll include the doc. retention tiers are configurable, we have a default 30-day and enterprise-tier 90/365 options.

[02:12] Emily Park: on the data side we can share a sanitized sample dataset but need to ensure no PHI flows out. prefer to run inference in our VPC with a private deployment if possible.
[02:25] Diego Alvarez: private deployment is supported - you'll get a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package if needed. for the pilot we usually start with a private VPC deployment in our dedicated pool so we can easily compare latency and cost.
[02:40] Maya Chen: just to clarify, for the POC we're proposing Redwood Dedicated resources in us-west2, with VPC peering to NexaHealth. that lets us hit the latency SLOs and also keeps data isolated.
[02:52] Rajesh Singh: do you have expected p95 numbers for a 2k token sequence on T5-like models?
[02:58] Diego Alvarez: p95 depends a lot on quantization and batching - ballpark on a g5-like profile we'd expect ~120-180ms p95 for short sequences, for 2k tokens it'll be higher, might be in the ~600-900ms range per token generation burst. that's why we want to run with your exact prompts.
[03:18] Emily Park: ok that's in the ballpark, our threshold is p95 < 800ms for interactive workflows.

[03:28] Maya Chen: action: Diego will run 3 benchmark prompts from Nexa's sample set in us-west2 and share numbers. Emily, can you share the sanitized samples after the call?
[03:37] Emily Park: yes, i'll drop them into the secure share, but will strip any PHI. target to share by Friday.
[03:44] Sophie Martin: on encryption - we need to confirm whether keys are customer managed and if at-rest data passes through Redwood-managed buckets.
[03:53] Diego Alvarez: we offer both CMK and Redwood-managed keys. for Private deployments we recommend CMK in the customer's KMS. model artifacts during pulls are encrypted in transit and at rest.
[04:05] Sophie Martin: okay we prefer CMK. please document the exact flow.

[04:12] Maya Chen: noted. i'll include KMS flow diagrams in the doc bundle.
[04:17] Rajesh Singh: small networking question: will we need to open 443 to control.redwood.io or can the connection be reverse-proxied from our side?
[04:26] Diego Alvarez: the control plane needs outbound 443 to control.redwood.io, but we can support a proxy if you require. main traffic for inference flows over the peered VPC and stays internal.

[04:40] Emily Park: perfect. one thing - cost. what's the expected per-token ballpark for this Dedicated config? we want to compare against our current self-hosted.
[04:49] Maya Chen: i'll share a cost model in the SOW, but high level Dedicated tends to be 15-30% cheaper than on-demand hosted depending on commit levels and batching. Redwood Optimize recommendations can often shave another 10-20% once we tune batching and quantization.
[05:05] Emily Park: sweet, we'll need that in writing to get internal approval.

[05:12] Sophie Martin: another security item: can you support SCIM or just SAML? we use SCIM for provisioning.
[05:20] Maya Chen: we support SAML for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning - i'll include SCIM endpoints and example payloads.

[05:30] Rajesh Singh: timeline check - if we get the VPC peering info by Monday can you run benchmarks mid-week?
[05:37] Diego Alvarez: yes, if we have samples and peering by Monday we can run tests Wednesday/Thursday.
[05:44] Maya Chen: recap of next steps: Maya send SAML/SOC2/SOW + KMS diagram by Friday, Diego run perf tests and share results by 2027-04-12, Emily share sanitized dataset by 2027-04-09, Rajesh validate peering by 2027-04-11.
[06:03] Emily Park: that works. thanks everyone.
[06:06] Maya Chen: thanks - i'll follow up in email with links to the doc bundle and a short checklist.
[06:12] Diego Alvarez: i'll attach the benchmark script and example config in the repo.
[06:18] Sophie Martin: we'll look at the SOC2 docs and get back with any gaps.
[06:22] Maya Chen: great, meeting over.

Notes: transcription has small mis-hears (control.redwood.io sometimes transcribed as control dot redwood eye oh), some speaker labels generic. Shared artifacts mentioned: link to pilot SOW (placeholder: https://redwood.com/sow/nexa-pilot), security pack (https://redwood.com/security/soc2), benchmark spreadsheet (internal link to be shared).
